subject: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@atlasdata.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@atlasdata.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot

Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Per our call I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) to get the pilot to a paid PoC and a staged commit. High level:

- Objective: Validate throughput and quality for AtlasData’s search ranking pipeline over a 6-week eval, then move into a 3-month ramp to an ongoing reserved commit.
- Evaluation (weeks 1–3): integration + perf tests, lightweight prompt set checks, baseline latency and cost profiling.
- Proof milestone (end wk3): AtlasData gets 50M validated production tokens; Redwood provides a performance report and a one-time engineering credit.
- Ramp (months 1–3 post-eval): proposed monthly TPM targets: 400M -> 1.1B -> 2.0B.
- Commercials: 3-month staged commit to hit long-term pricing. Proposed committed TPM (post-ramp): 6B total over 9 months. Discount triggers: 12% off list at signed commit; additional 6% uplift if 6B sustained for 12 months.

Attached: AtlasData_MAP_v3.pdf (MAP draft), SOW_AtlasData_v1.docx (ops scope), pricing-sheet-atlas.csv (costing).

Ask: Please review and confirm whether the ramp profile is acceptable or if you prefer a softer Month1 (we can propose 250M month1 with a slightly longer ramp). Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to finalize timing.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Li <evan.li@atlasdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@atlasdata.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the MAP. A few clarifications from our side before we lock timelines:

1) Month1 target looks aggressive for our internal rollout. Can we soften Month1 to 250M tokens and extend ramp to 4 months (250M -> 700M -> 1.6B -> 2.4B)?
2) Pricing: we like the staged discount idea, but procurement needs clearer language on when discounts apply (commit signed vs. sustained usage).
3) Security/compliance: procurement asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence and clarification on data residency — can you share your SOC 2 report and confirm hosted region?
4) Contract timing: our legal prefers a single SOW + master services agreement; they’ll route through a third-party contracts reviewer (CloudLaw).

We’re available for a 30-min sync Fri 10/23 at 09:30 PT if that works — want to get to a clean commercial baseline before legal starts redlines.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Li
Head of Product Engineering, AtlasData
evan.li@atlasdata.com | +1 646-555-0134

[Referenced: procurement@atlasdata.com]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot — external asks (softening Month1 & SOC2)

Team —

Forwarding Evan’s reply. Key asks: soften Month1 to 250M and extend ramp to 4 months; procurement needs SOC 2 and hosted-region confirmation; legal will involve CloudLaw. They want clearer discount trigger language.

My read: AtlasData is committed to proving thier workload but wants lower short-term risk. Proposed counter:
- Accept softened month1: 250M -> month2 700M -> month3 1.6B -> month4 2.4B.
- Offer a structured commit: if they sign a 9-month committed profile (target 6B tokens total), apply 10% off list on committed volume day-1 and an additional 5% if they sustain >=70% of target for three consecutive months.
- Provide SOC 2 Type II report and confirm region (US-West) — ops can supply by EOD tomorrow.
- Ask legal to accept standard Redwood MSA + SOW with CloudLaw review; propose DocuSign route.

Action items:
- Karthik: please model the revised pricing with this concession and share a pricing-sheet we can send to Evan (include clear discount trigger language).
- Marissa: prep quick call agenda for Fri 9:30 PT (30m) focused on MAP alignment and legal path.
- Lauren: flag if the discount levels need senior approval (I set a floor at 10% at signing + 5% performance).

Thanks —
Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot — pricing proposal

Ben / team —

Thanks — ran the numbers based on the softened ramp and Ben’s suggested commercial concession. Summary (high level):

- Ramp (agreed): Month1 250M | Month2 700M | Month3 1.6B | Month4 2.4B.
- Committed anchor: 9-month contract targeting 6B tokens total post-eval.
- Pricing model: list price token unit x; commit discount at signature: 10% off committed tokens. If AtlasData sustains >=70% of the monthly committed target for 3 consecutive months, apply an additional 5% rebate on the following invoice period.
- One-time credits: engineering credits equal to 1% of first-quarter committed value if proof milestone met end of eval.
- Legal/Proc: CloudLaw will be sent the MSA + SOW; procurement wants SOC 2 — Ops will attach.

I attached a revised pricing-sheet that splits committed vs overage pricing and includes a worked example for month-by-month invoices. If acceptable we can push this to Evan after Lauren confirms the discount floor.

Notes: the additional 5% rebate is effectively a performance-based incentive to encourage ramp velocity while protecting Redwood’s unit economics. If Lauren wants lower downside, we can instead make it a one-time rebate rather than ongoing.

Karthik
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

[Attachment: pricing-sheet-atlas.csv (csv)]

Subject: RE: Proposed MAP & ramp for AtlasData pilot — final commercial baseline and next steps

Evan / Priya —

Thanks for the call last Friday. Per our discussion and internal alignment, here’s the commercial baseline and MAP steps we agreed. Please review and confirm so we can route to legal for a quick MSA + SOW execution (DocuSign link below).

MAP & commercial summary:
- Eval (wk1–3): integration + perf; proof milestone: 50M validated production tokens and performance report.
- Agreed ramp: Month1 250M | Month2 700M | Month3 1.6B | Month4 2.4B.
- Committed anchor: 9-month commitment post-eval targeting 6B tokens total.
- Pricing: 10% off list applied to committed volume on signature. Performance rebate: additional 5% applied if AtlasData sustains >=70% of monthly target for 3 consecutive months (rebate applied to subsequent invoice).
- One-time engineering credit: applied if proof milestone is met at end of eval.

Operational asks:
- Redwood Ops will provide SOC 2 Type II report and confirm US-West hosting by EOD tomorrow.
- Please provide CloudLaw contact for routing the redlines.

Next steps:
1) AtlasData to confirm the ramp profile and the commercial language above by reply.
2) Redwood to send clean MSA + SOW via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/xyz-sign/ATL-0884
3) Upon signature, onboarding will kick off and Ops will schedule the integration window.

We’ve attached the final MAP PDF and the SOW draft for reference. If this looks good, please indicate approval and we’ll send the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks and looking forward —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
